hypothesis: Free weather forecasts, converted into decisions, earn no more after costs than the same decisions without a forecast or with climatology only.

signals.NAT_netload_13: demand-weighted six-region net-load anomaly (demand - wind - solar, forecast minus climatology, % of climatological demand), mean over leads 1-3
signals.NAT_demand_17: demand-weighted six-region demand anomaly, mean over leads 1-7
signals.ERCO_netload_17: ERCOT net-load anomaly, mean over leads 1-7
signals.NAT_lowwind_17: minus the demand-weighted wind anomaly (low wind = long), mean over leads 1-7
signals.PJM_demand_13: PJM demand anomaly, mean over leads 1-3
signals.TWIN_ramp_17: climatology twin: climatological net load over the coming 7 days minus the previous 7 days (the seasonal ramp; no forecast information)

standardisation: centred on the expanding mean and scaled by the expanding standard deviation of all earlier values of the signal (history from the 2026-06-01 backfill included), at least 60 observations
timing: signal from the 00z IFS cycle of the issue date; position entered at that day's close and earned from the next trading day; issue dates that are not trading days are skipped
evidence_of_edge: Reviewed at [60, 125, 250] trading days. Evidence of an edge only if, at the review, the equal-weight weather family has a positive annualised net return, exceeds the climatology twin family, has a positive beta-adjusted mean-difference alpha against SPY, and is positive in both halves of the sample. Otherwise: no evidence of an edge.
mechanics_check: The scoring code was exercised on 2026-08-15 to 2026-10-09 data to test the mechanics only; those days are not part of the test and no rule was changed after seeing them, except that signals are centred (see standardisation) after an uncentred version was found to stay long almost all the time.
not_claimed: No result is tested for statistical significance, and a null result is not proof that no edge exists anywhere, only that none shows up in this registered set.
